Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. BlueRiver's audit team has asked us to collect a compact evidence packet for SIG v1.1 and CAIQ that focuses on the networking/isolation story for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they want: 

- A short narrative describing the "tenant corridor" concept (how traffic flows are segmented end-to-end across control, data and management planes).
- Network diagrams (high-level and a zoomed-in service-corridor view) that show tenant boundary enforcement, egress controls, and control-plane access patterns.
- A proof matrix that maps specific SIG/CAIQ controls to artifacts (config, logs, diagrams).
- Any SOC 2-relevant callouts for our scope (data in transit boundaries, key management, audit logs).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a compact packet (PDF + diagrams + spreadsheet) by next week (target 14 Jun)? If you have a recommended filename structure for the artifacts that helps our intake team, please include that.

Also useful: callouts about runtime mechanisms (KV cache isolation, model-variant routing, and fallback behavior when a tenant's dedicated pool is saturated).

Thanks — we may redline a few items but want the base packet to attach to our SIG intake.

Claire Thompson

Quick technical summary (for the matrix and diagram):

1) Corridor concept (short):
- Management corridor: control-plane traffic (deploy API, rollouts, telemetry ingestion) isolated into a private control plane per-customer for Private deployments; dedicated control namespaces for Dedicated. Access gated via MFA + short-lived certs.
- Data corridor: inference request/response path. Tenant isolation achieved via network ACLs + per-tenant ingress endpoints in Dedicated pools, and prefix-based KV cache shard isolation in all modes.
- Service corridor (east-west): internal service-to-service calls (batching, embedding compute); routed through segmented VPCs and enforcement via service mesh policies (mTLS + RBAC).

2) Runtime fencing details (to include in narrative):
- KV cache isolation: keys are namespace-prefixed using tenant_id and ephemeral salts; cache eviction respects tenant quotas and is scoped per-pool to avoid leakage.
- Model routing and fallbacks: requests route to tenant's pinned model variant; when capacity constrained, router downgrades to compatible quantized variant in lower-cost pool (policy documented) and logs the event to audit log (audit: routing_decision.*).
- Egress control: DNAT + centralized proxy for Private; explicit egress allowlists per-tenant for Dedicated.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS integration for Private (HSM-backed key wrap). Hosted uses Redwood KMS with separate key buckets per tenant and strict IAM scoping.

3) Artifacts I'm attaching (first pass):
- tenant_corridor_diagram_v1.png [attachment: tenant_corridor_diagram_v1.png (image/png)]
- segmentation-proof-matrix.xlsx [attachment: segmentation-proof-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Notes for the diagram: the zoomed view highlights the three corridors, control-plane egress points, a notional firewall rule set snippet for tenant boundary enforcement, and the KMS trust boundary.

I'll paste a short route-policy snippet for the matrix:

---
route-policy:
- match: tenant_id == {T} && model_variant in tenant_allowed_variants
  action: route_to_pool(tenant_pool_id)
- else: route_to_pool(shared_fallback_pool) ; emit_audit(event="fallback_route")
---
